# Commit Message Standards

Good commit messages make the history useful. They explain *why* a change was made, not just *what* changed.

---

## Format

```
<type>: <short description>

<optional body — explain why, not what>
```

---

## Types

| Type | When to use |
|------|-------------|
| `feat` | New feature |
| `fix` | Bug fix |
| `refactor` | Code restructuring without behaviour change |
| `test` | Adding or updating tests |
| `docs` | Documentation changes |
| `chore` | Maintenance, dependency updates, tooling |
| `perf` | Performance improvements |

---

## Good vs Poor Examples

**Good:**
```
fix: prevent duplicate records on pipeline retry

Idempotency key was not being checked before insert,
causing duplicates when the pipeline retried on timeout.
```

**Poor:**
```
fix bug
```
